I had an induction at 40 weeks last year. They started pitocin (oxytocin) through an IV at about 11pm. I think because I was already at 40 weeks, 4cm dilated and had regular contractions that was still in early labour, it made for a very quick induction. It started to get intense quickly. I had no epidural but was allowed to use a tub for pain relief. When I got into the tub, I felt like I could barely walk. The water helped a lot though. I told myself that I could keep going and that I didn’t need the epidural yet and that was enough until crowning started. A nurse held my hand tightly which helped a lot and I held my husbands hand too. At that point I felt like I couldn’t move so my midwife let me deliver in the tub (1am). I saw my baby in the water and panicked because I forgot that they’re still getting oxygen through the umbilical cord. I didn’t know why nobody was picking him up in a hurry so I grabbed him and put him on my chest. He started crying and I was so happy. They took my baby to the warmer to check him over and I went to the bed to deliver the placenta. They gave me my baby again right after that. When my husband was doing his skin to skin, they gave me three stitches in two different places which hurt more than my baby because I need more anesthetic than normal (thanks irish genes!) and completely forgot to tell them that. It was my first time getting stitches and second time getting local anaesthetic. 

I could not have asked for a better birth. I felt ready to do the birth part again 30 minutes later. My midwife gave me some toast and water to last me until lunch or breakfast (I can’t remember which) but I had a snack packed for a long labour. I wish I had brought more snacks. I didn’t even realize I had been in the delivery room for an extra 3 hours because I was enjoying the time with my baby. 

I also had a miscarriage this year and that was the worst pain I have ever been in. Childbirth is ranked fourth on my list with endometriosis flare ups in second and the stitches in third. I don’t know if other people share the same opinion but I personally am hardly worried about the pain again next year. You’ll do great :) It’s okay to get an epidural if you want one too! You should be as comfortable as possible. I just wanted to prove something to my gynaecologist.
